answer.rationale: The situation most closely mirrors memory_b1: a release was deployed (2 hours ago) and a write-path error/latency spike followed. memory_b1 records that rollback cleared the checkout spike with no customer impact. Meanwhile memory_b5 tells us that routing reports to read replicas helped dashboard load but would not address a *write-path* p99 degradation—which is the core problem here. Settlement traffic is at its daily peak, so losing writes is unacceptable; rollback to the prior known-stable build is the intervention with the highest expected value: it directly removes the suspected cause (the 2-hour-old release) and memory_b1 confirms the rollback itself completed without customer impact. Regional failover, adding capacity, circuit breakers, and read-replica routing each address different failure modes (network degradation, saturation, partner outage, and read-heavy load respectively) and do not match the correlated release-plus-write-latency pattern observed. Because settlement writes are heavy, I request the rollback be executed as a small guarded test (one shard/cell first, confirm p99 recovers, then sweep remaining nodes) to preserve uncertainty about whether this release truly is the culprit rather than the daily peak alone.
